```{r setup}
library(netz)
library(ggplot2)
library(malariasimulation)
```

In [malariasimulation](https://mrc-ide.github.io/malariasimulation/) we can 
implement the [bed net intervention](https://mrc-ide.github.io/malariasimulation/articles/VectorControl.html)
by specifying the % of the population who are distributed a bed net 
(and assumed to use it) at given time points.

We often want to match malariasimulation distributions so that they result
in an observed time-series of usage that we have data for. The netz package
can help us to do this. As 

netz provides two functions to achieve this:

* `usage_to_model_distribution()`: estimates malariasimulation distribution inputs required to achieve target usage rates.
* `model_distribution_to_usage()`: estimates the usage rates over time for a given   set of distributions.

These functions assume _random_ correlation between recipients. The period a net is retained for is set with the  `net_loss_function` argument. Both malariasimulation and netz supports the following two net retention functions:

* `net_loss_exp()`: exponential net loss, set with `mean_retention`.
* `net_loss_map()`: logistic (smooth-compact) net loss, set with `half_life` and `k`. This functional form is in line with that from the paper by Bertozzi-Villa et al.


```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# Create some example usage data
data <- data.frame(
  year = 2000:2009,
  usage = c(0, 0.02, 0.03, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.7)
)

## We assume that
## Usage is measured at the mid point of the year
## Distributions occur at the start of the year
usage_timesteps = (data$year - 2000) * 365 + 1 + (365 / 2)
distribution_timesteps = (data$year - 2000) * 365 + 1

# Simulation settings 
year <- 365
sim_length <- 10 * year
human_population <- 5000
starting_EIR <- 1
n_dist <- length(distribution_timesteps)


# Estimate model usage over time to validate
pred <- data.frame(
  t <- 1:sim_length
)
```

## Exponential net retention

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}

# Estimate model inputs to achieve observed usage
data$model_input_exp <- usage_to_model_distribution(
  usage = data$usage,
  usage_timesteps = usage_timesteps,
  distribution_timesteps = distribution_timesteps,
  net_loss_function = net_loss_exp,
  mean_retention = 700
)

# Estimate model usage over time
pred$model_usage_exp <- model_distribution_to_usage(
  usage_timesteps = pred$t,
  distribution = data$model_input_exp,
  distribution_timesteps = distribution_timesteps,
  net_loss_function = net_loss_exp,
  mean_retention = 700
)

set.seed(123)

simparams_exp <- get_parameters(
  list(human_population = human_population)
) |>
  set_equilibrium(init_EIR = starting_EIR) |>
  set_bednets(
    timesteps = distribution_timesteps,
    coverages = data$model_input_exp,
    retention = 700,
    dn0 = matrix(rep(0.5, n_dist), nrow = n_dist, ncol = 1),
    rn = matrix(rep(0.4, n_dist), nrow = n_dist, ncol = 1),
    rnm = matrix(rep(0.3, n_dist), nrow = n_dist, ncol = 1),
    gamman = rep(2.64 * 365, n_dist)
  )

validate_exp <- run_simulation(timesteps = sim_length, parameters = simparams_exp)
validate_exp$model_use <- validate_exp$n_use_net / human_population

ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    data = pred,
    aes(x = 2000 + (t / 365), y = model_usage_exp)
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = validate_exp,
    aes(x = 2000 + (timestep / 365), y = model_use),
    col = "forestgreen"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = data,
    aes(x = year + 0.5, y = usage),
    col = "darkred",
    size = 2
  ) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Model usage", title = "Exponential") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2000:2010) +
  theme_classic()

```

In some cases, the function may struggle to fit the usage observations 
well. This may especially be the case if we are uncertain about bed net parameters,
such as the rate of net loss, or if early data points are spurious.

## Logistic (smooth-compact) net retention

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}

# Estimate model inputs to achieve observed usage
data$model_input_map <- usage_to_model_distribution(
  usage = data$usage,
  usage_timesteps = usage_timesteps,
  distribution_timesteps = distribution_timesteps,
  net_loss_function = net_loss_map,
  half_life = 700 * log(2), # To have same mean_reation as exp example
  k = 20
)

# Estimate model usage over time
pred$model_usage_map <- model_distribution_to_usage(
  usage_timesteps = pred$t,
  distribution = data$model_input_map,
  distribution_timesteps = distribution_timesteps,
  net_loss_function = net_loss_map,
  half_life = 700 * log(2), 
  k = 20
)

set.seed(123)

simparams_map <- get_parameters(
  list(human_population = human_population)
) |>
  set_equilibrium(init_EIR = starting_EIR) |>
  set_bednets(
    timesteps = distribution_timesteps,
    coverages = data$model_input_map,
    logistic_half_life = 700 * log(2),
    logistic_k = 20,
    dn0 = matrix(rep(0.5, n_dist), nrow = n_dist, ncol = 1),
    rn = matrix(rep(0.4, n_dist), nrow = n_dist, ncol = 1),
    rnm = matrix(rep(0.3, n_dist), nrow = n_dist, ncol = 1),
    gamman = rep(2.64 * 365, n_dist)
  )

validate_map <- run_simulation(timesteps = sim_length, parameters = simparams_map)
validate_map$model_use <- validate_map$n_use_net / human_population

ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    data = pred,
    aes(x = 2000 + (t / 365), y = model_usage_map)
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = validate_map,
    aes(x = 2000 + (timestep / 365), y = model_use),
    col = "forestgreen"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = data,
    aes(x = year + 0.5, y = usage),
    col = "darkred",
    size = 2
  ) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Model usage", title = "Logistic") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2000:2010) +
  theme_classic()

```
